body:
The observation-cursor behaviour that applies to this integration is the one of the pinned @ordarium/* 1.3.1 line: a durable state-change-feed cursor exists and its invalidation is FAIL-CLOSED. The 1.2.0 commentary's "no change-feed cursor / no cursor-invalidation failure" does NOT apply to this integration.

Decisive provenance: docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md self-declares "historical, superseded by later releases" and "Anything here applies only to the 1.2.0 line" - explicit version scope + explicit supersession, so it is not co-applicable here. The workspace's binding integration sources are its manifests and installed artifacts, which are all 1.3.1: package.json:32-34 (core/ledger-sqlite/host-kit) and :37 (testing) pin ordarium-v1.3.1; pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18 overrides mirror 1.3.1; node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite,host-kit}/package.json all report version 1.3.1. Stale 1.0.0/1.2.0 mentions in README.md:26, docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md and docker/minimal/README.md are descriptive/lagging, not version scopes on this pin.

Applicable 1.3.1 semantics (evidence in pinned artifacts):
- OrdariumStateStore.changes(filter?, cursor?) is exposed as "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)", gated by supportsStateChangeFeed (capability stateChangeFeed === true + a changes method); a ledger lacking it fails closed with LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED (core state.d.ts/state.js). This integration's ledger is the crash-durable SqliteLedger, which declares stateChangeFeed: true (ledger-sqlite index.js capabilities); src/effects/runtime.ts constructs it and exposes the store via createStateStore({runtime}).
- The cursor is opaque (base64url of {"c":"<digits>"}), a global, filter-independent durable position (ordarium_state_changes.change_seq) delivered in ascending commit-observation order (core types.d.ts StateChangePage/StateChangeFeed; ledger-sqlite changes()).
- StateChangePage.cursor is always present, unlike the optional nextCursor of other read surfaces: reaching the end of the feed still yields a durable resume position, with hasMore indicating further matching changes.
- Invalidation failure applies: an undecodable/foreign cursor -> InvalidCursorError; a cursor above the ledger high-water mark (restored/replaced/corrupt ledger) -> InvalidCursorError, i.e. fail closed rather than silently restarting from the beginning of the feed (core errors.d.ts InvalidCursorError; ledger-sqlite changes() semantic check "a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed"). Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected.

Honest caveat: Palimpsest's current telemetry load uses store.list() pagination (optional nextCursor), not changes() (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts). The observation-cursor semantics above are nonetheless the pinned integration's contract and govern whenever the state change feed is exercised against it.

Local provenance analysis (version scope + explicit supersession) is sufficient to settle the manifest-vs-commentary conflict, so no peer contact was needed.
